lastCompletedGameRecap.recapHeadline: McCaffrey's TDs of 74 and 66 yards and Samuel's 70-yard score help 49ers beat Cowboys 46-40
lastCompletedGameRecap.recapLeadExcerpt: ARLINGTON, Texas -- — Christian McCaffrey 's first long touchdown catch was straight out of the schoolyard, the second a Kyle Shanahan special for the San Francisco 49ers .  Throw in a reverse to Deebo Samuel that completely fooled the Dallas defense, and you have close to the most yards gained and allowed in the history of two proud franchises.  Brock Purdy threw TD passes of 74 and 66 yards to McCaffrey, Samuel ran 70 yards for a score in front of his own sideline and the 49ers beat the Cowboys 46-40 on Sunday.  The Cowboys had cut a 19-point deficit in the second half to six in the final four minutes when McCaffrey ran away from edge rusher Von Miller on third down, caught a pass over the middle and sprinted untouched to the end zone for the second time. “It really is backyard football at that point,” said McCaffrey, whose 223 scrimmage yards included a career-best 161 receiving and a 16-yard score among his 62 rushing yards.  Dak Prescott tied his career high with five TD passes, and George Pickens caught a career-high three for the Cowboys (4-6), who fell short again in trying to win consecutive games under second-year coach Brian Schottenheimer. irReserve.name: Demond Claiborne
irReserve.beatNote: Claiborne suffered a knee injury during a recent practice. While head coach Kevin O'Connell stated he doesn't believe Claiborne will require surgery, the injury is severe enough to keep him off the field for at least four games. The 23-year-old hasn't done much from a statistical standpoint throughout the 2026 campaign, amassing just 13 yards off six carries while garnering two catches for eight yards.

irReserve.name: Jordan Addison
irReserve.beatNote: O'Connell indicated that Addison will be a candidate for injured reserve, though if he does end up being deactivated, the Vikings anticipate that the wideout would be able to return after sitting out the minimum four games. Addison injured his thumb at Friday's practice and subsequently was inactive for Sunday's 30-10 win over Green Bay. For as long as Addison is sidelined, Jauan Jennings (calf), Myles Price and Tai Felton will be the options to see added reps behind No. 1 receiver Justin Jefferson.

irReserve.name: Donovan Jackson
irReserve.beatNote: Jackson suffered a torn meniscus during Sunday's 15-10 win over Miami, and he was already set to miss the rest of the regular season, so Tuesday's move to the IR comes as no surprise. Joe Huber is the top candidate to take over as Minnesota's starting left guard in Jackson's absence.

irReserve.name: Josh Oliver
irReserve.beatNote: Oliver's move to IR was expected after the tight end was diagnosed with a torn bicep Monday. The tight end will likely miss most, if not all, of the 2026 season as he recovers from surgery. T.J. Hockenson and Gavin Bartholomew are now the only tight ends on the Vikings' roster, meaning practice-squad elevations ahead of Week 4 will likely include at least one more option at the position. The Vikings signed linebacker Kyle Van Noy to the 53-man roster in a corresponding move.

irReserve.name: Dwight McGlothern Jr.
irReserve.beatNote: 4-game minimum satisfied on Injured Reserve (Undisclosed); awaiting 21-day practice window designation.

irReserve.name: Nick Samac
irReserve.beatNote: Samac appeared on the Vikings' injury report during Week 3 prep with a new knee injury. The backup center's issue must be significant, as he was promptly moved to IR. Samac will need to miss at least four games on IR before becoming eligible to return to the Vikings' active roster.

coachingMatchup.headline: Kyle Shanahan & DC Raheem Morris vs. Minnesota Vikings HC Kevin O'Connell, OC Wes Phillips, DC Brian Flores
coachingMatchup.summary: San Francisco (8-1) brings the NFL's #1 Offensive EPA unit (+12.28/gm) and #1 Rush EPA defense (-2.49/gm) into a contrasting coordinator duel against Minnesota Vikings (7-2) and HC Kevin O'Connell, OC Wes Phillips, DC Brian Flores. Shanahan's play-calling script centers on 21 personnel and pre-snap motion to dictate box counts, while Raheem Morris's split-safety rotations cap explosive plays (3.1/gm, #1 NFL).
bullets: Pass-Game Efficiency & Coverage Shell Delta: Entering #2 in Passing EPA/game (+9.35) and #8 in Sack Rate Allowed (4.7%), Shanahan uses condensed splits, jet motion, and orbit motion to force DC Brian Flores to tip single-high vs. two-high rotations pre-snap before attacking the intermediate honey-hole between hook/curl and curl/flat defenders on play-action choice/dagger and boot flood concepts.

Trench Run-Fit & Box-Count Chess: Against OC Wes Phillips's early-down run script (#29 Rushing EPA)—mixing pin-and-pull, counter, and duo targeting the A- and B-gaps—Morris anchors light boxes (#2 at 3.41 yds/carry allowed) while disguising Quarters, Cover 6, and cloud-trap shells behind a Wide-9 four-man rush.

Money-Down & Red-Zone Execution: SF converts 52.0% of 3rd downs (#1) and 82.8% of red-zone trips (#1) versus MIN's #3 3rd-down defense (31.1%) and #1 red-zone TD rate allowed (25.0%), giving Shanahan clear 4th-and-short go-for-it leverage inside plus territory.

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Brock Purdy, George Kittle & Keenan Allen vs. Vikings Seam & Slot Coverage
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Brock Purdy pairs George Kittle's intermediate seam/over separation with Keenan Allen's veteran slot option routes between the numbers, forcing Minnesota Vikings's linebackers into constant high-low conflict.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch Kittle (#85) and Allen align in reduced splits on 3rd-and-medium—whichever defender widens with motion opens the inward-breaking dagger or option sit route.

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Nick Bosa, DeForest Buckner & Osa Odighizuwa vs. Kirk Cousins & Vikings O-Line
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: SF: Buckner + Odighizuwa 6.0 Sacks, 21 Pressures | MIN: 9.2% Sack Rate (#27)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Aligning DeForest Buckner and Osa Odighizuwa as 3-tech and 2i penetrators forces Minnesota Vikings's center and guards to honor interior A/B-gap T-E stunts, isolating Nick Bosa 1-on-1 on the Wide-9 edge against Kirk Cousins.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Key the opposing center's slide protection on 3rd-and-long—sliding inside toward Buckner (#99) leaves Bosa (#97) singled up on the edge.

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Renardo Green, Deommodore Lenoir & Fred Warner vs. Kirk Cousins & Justin Jefferson
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: SF: Green 4 INT (61.6 Rtg) · Warner 76 Tkl, 4 FF | MIN: #23 Pass EPA
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Deommodore Lenoir sliding into the nickel slot alongside Renardo Green outside and Fred Warner patrolling deep middle crossers challenges Kirk Cousins's primary timing windows to Justin Jefferson.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch Lenoir (#2) bump inside in nickel on 3rd-and-4-to-7 while Warner (#54) disguises middle-hook depth until the snap.

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Christian McCaffrey & Kyle Juszczyk vs. Vikings Second-Level Run Fits
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: SF: #1 Rush EPA (+2.93/gm) | MIN: 111.9 yds/Gm Allowed (#17)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Christian McCaffrey stretches horizontal edges on outside zone behind Kyle Juszczyk before punishing over-pursuing linebackers on backside B-gap cutbacks and angle/Texas choice routes.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: When Juszczyk (#44) inserts weakside off pre-snap motion, look for McCaffrey (#23) pressing the frontside C-gap before planting vertical in one cut.

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Trent Williams, Dominick Puni & Jake Brendel vs. Eric Wilson & Vikings Pass Rush
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: SF: 4.7% Sack Rate Allowed (#8) | MIN: 4.11 Sacks/Gm (#1)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: LT Trent Williams locking down the blindside solo allows C Jake Brendel and RG Dominick Puni to sustain interior combo-blocks and slide protection against Eric Wilson.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch whether SF leaves Trent Williams (#71) on a true island without TE chip help so George Kittle (#85) can release cleanly into intermediate routes.
